body: I think I like "popover trigger", and that's what's in the current PR. So just a comment that the commit description needs to be updated accordingly.
ElementPopover is a bit confusing IMO, since the input & button aren't the popovers themselves

@keithamus mentioned in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11383#issuecomment-3180105448 that the name was chosen to align with `ElementContentEditable`.

The mixin has the attributes `popoverTargetElement` and `popoverTargetAction` (not `popover`) so if we want to align with that how about `ElementPopoverTarget`?

FWIW, I've gone with `ElementInterestFor` in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11006, and I think this would all be consistent enough.

(Fortunately the names of mixins aren't web exposed, so we can change it again later.)

ElementContentEditable makes sense since they're literally the properties that make an element contenteditable. But ElementPopover doesn't, because these aren't the properties that make an element a popover.

Maybe `ElementPopoverSource` ? `ElementPopoverTarget` also doesn't make a lot of sense in this context because popovertarget refers to the targeted popover, rather than the element that invoked the popover.

`ElementInterestSource` would probably make more sense than `ElementInterestFor` 

(Not sure if we should aim for consistency with `ElementContentEditable` here tbh though)

Anyway, hopefully my rationale makes some sense here
We call them the popover target attributes so I'd be fine with going with `PopoverTargetAttributes`.
Just to be clear you want for e.g. `HTMLInputElement includes PopoverTargetAttributes`?
